explanation.title: Spanish Reflexive Verbs: When the Subject Acts on Itself

sections.subtitle: Reflexive Pronouns & Basic Usage
sections.content:
📋 Reflexive Pronouns

✅ The Pronouns:
• me (myself)
• te (yourself)
• se (himself/herself/itself/themselves)
• nos (ourselves)
• os (yourselves - Spain)
• se (yourselves - formal/Latin America)

📍 Pronoun Placement:

1️⃣ Before conjugated verb:
→ Me lavo (I wash myself)
→ Te duchas (You shower)
→ Se viste (He/She gets dressed)

2️⃣ Attached to infinitive OR before conjugated verb:
→ Voy a lavarme / Me voy a lavar
  (I'm going to wash myself)

3️⃣ Attached to gerund OR before conjugated verb:
→ Estoy lavándome / Me estoy lavando
  (I'm washing myself)

4️⃣ Affirmative command (attached):
→ ¡Lávate! (Wash yourself!)

5️⃣ Negative command (before):
→ ¡No te laves! (Don't wash yourself!)

sections.subtitle: Common Reflexive Verbs
sections.content:
📋 Essential Reflexive Verbs

🌅 Daily Routine:
• levantarse (get up)
• despertarse (wake up)
• ducharse (shower)
• bañarse (bathe)
• lavarse (wash)
• vestirse (get dressed)
• peinarse (comb hair)
• afeitarse (shave)
• maquillarse (put on makeup)
• acostarse (go to bed)

📍 Position/Movement:
• sentarse (sit down)
• levantarse (stand up)
• pararse (stop/stand)
• irse (leave/go away)
• quedarse (stay)

😊 Emotion/State:
• sentirse (feel)
• ponerse (become/put on)
• enojarse (get angry)
• preocuparse (worry)
• aburrirse (get bored)
• divertirse (have fun)
• alegrarse (be happy)

💡 Examples:
→ Me despierto a las 7 (I wake up at 7)
→ Nos divertimos mucho (We have a lot of fun)

sections.subtitle: Reciprocal Actions & Pronominal Verbs
sections.content:
📋 Reciprocal Use (Each Other)

✅ Formation:
• Use nos, os, se (plural subjects only)
• Means 'each other'

💡 Examples:
→ Nos vemos mañana (We'll see each other tomorrow)
→ Se aman (They love each other)
→ Os escribís (You write to each other)

📍 Context clarifies reciprocal vs reflexive

⚠️ PRONOMINAL VERBS
(Change meaning with reflexive pronoun)

💡 ir (go) → irse (leave/go away):
→ Voy a Madrid (I'm going to Madrid)
→ Me voy (I'm leaving)

💡 dormir (sleep) → dormirse (fall asleep):
→ Duermo 8 horas (I sleep 8 hours)
→ Me duermo rápido (I fall asleep quickly)

✅ Other Examples:
• poner (put) → ponerse (put on/become)
• acordar (agree) → acordarse (remember)
• parecer (seem) → parecerse (resemble)
• quedar (remain) → quedarse (stay)

sections.subtitle: Accidental/Unintentional Se
sections.content:
📋 Expressing Accidents (It Just Happened!)

✅ Structure:
• se + indirect object pronoun + verb (3rd person)

🎯 Purpose:
Removes blame/responsibility - shows action was accidental

💡 Examples:

→ Se me olvidó la tarea
  (I forgot the homework - lit: homework forgot itself to me)

→ Se te cayó el libro
  (You dropped the book - accidentally)

→ Se nos perdieron las llaves
  (We lost the keys - they got lost on us)

→ Se le rompió el vaso
  (He/She broke the glass - accidentally)

→ Se me acabó el dinero
  (I ran out of money - it ran out on me)

⚠️ Common Verbs:
• olvidarse (forget)
• caerse (fall/drop)
• perderse (get lost)
• romperse (break)
• acabarse (run out)
• ocurrirse (occur to)

😊 Benefit:
Shows it wasn't intentional - removes responsibility!

sections.subtitle: Passive Se Constructions
sections.content:
📋 Passive Se (No Agent Named)

✅ Structure:
• se + verb (3rd person) + subject
• Verb agrees with subject

💡 Examples:

→ Se habla español
  (Spanish is spoken - lit: One speaks Spanish)

→ Se venden casas
  (Houses are sold/for sale)

→ Se necesitan trabajadores
  (Workers are needed)

→ Se prohibe fumar
  (Smoking is prohibited)

📋 Agreement Rules:

Singular subject → singular verb:
→ Se vende casa (House for sale)

Plural subject → plural verb:
→ Se venden casas (Houses for sale)

🎯 Common Uses:
• Signs
• Instructions
• Formal writing
• General statements

💡 More Examples:
→ Se ruega silencio (Silence is requested)
→ Se alquilan habitaciones (Rooms for rent)
→ Se busca persona (Person wanted)

sections.subtitle: Impersonal Se
sections.content:
📋 Impersonal Se (One/You/People)

✅ Structure:
• se + verb (singular only)
• No specific subject
• General 'one/you/people'

💡 Examples:

→ Se come bien aquí
  (One eats well here / The food is good here)

→ Se vive bien en España
  (One lives well in Spain / Life is good in Spain)

→ Se trabaja mucho
  (People work a lot)

→ Se dice que...
  (It is said that... / People say that...)

⚡ Critical Rule:
ALWAYS singular verb, even with plural objects

📋 Impersonal vs Passive Se:

✅ IMPERSONAL (no subject):
• Always singular verb
→ Se necesita trabajar (One needs to work)
  (trabajar = infinitive, not subject)

⚠️ PASSIVE (has subject):
• Verb agrees with subject
→ Se necesita experiencia (Experience is needed)
  (experiencia = subject)

💡 Key Difference:
Impersonal has NO SUBJECT
Passive has subject that verb agrees with

questions.question: What are the reflexive pronouns in Spanish?

answers.text: me, te, se, nos, os, se
yo, tú, él, nosotros, vosotros, ellos
mi, ti, si, nuestro, vuestro, su
lo, la, le, los, las, les

questions.hint: These pronouns mean 'myself, yourself, himself, ourselves', etc.

questions.question: Where do reflexive pronouns go with conjugated verbs?
questions.hint: Me lavo, te duchas, se viste - pronoun comes before conjugated verb.

questions.question: 'Me lavo' means...
questions.hint: Me = myself. The subject performs the action on themselves.

questions.question: 'Voy a lavarme' or 'Me voy a lavar' - which is correct?
questions.hint: With infinitive, pronoun can attach to infinitive OR go before conjugated verb.

questions.question: What is the affirmative tú command of 'lavarse' (wash yourself)?
questions.hint: Affirmative command: attach pronoun to end (lava + te = lávate).

questions.question: What is the negative tú command of 'lavarse' (don't wash yourself)?
questions.hint: Negative command: pronoun goes before verb (no + te + laves).

questions.question: 'Me despierto a las 7' means...
questions.hint: Despertarse = to wake up (reflexive). Me despierto = I wake myself up.

questions.question: 'Nos divertimos mucho' means...

answers.text: We have a lot of fun (ourselves)

questions.hint: Divertirse = to have fun (reflexive). Nos = ourselves.

questions.question: 'Nos vemos mañana' - What does this mean?
questions.hint: Plural reflexive pronouns can mean 'each other' (reciprocal action).

questions.question: 'Se aman' means...
questions.hint: Plural 'se' can be reciprocal: they love each other.

questions.question: 'Voy a Madrid' vs 'Me voy' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Voy = I'm going (to place); Me voy = I'm leaving (general)
Voy is past, Me voy is present

questions.hint: Irse (pronominal) changes meaning: 'to leave/go away' not just 'go'.

questions.question: 'Duermo 8 horas' vs 'Me duermo rápido' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Duermo = I sleep; Me duermo = I fall asleep
Duermo is formal, Me duermo is informal

questions.hint: Dormirse (pronominal) = fall asleep. Dormir = sleep (state).

questions.question: 'Se me olvidó la tarea' literally translates to...

answers.text: The homework forgot itself to me (I forgot the homework)
I forgot the homework on purpose

questions.hint: Accidental se construction removes blame - it 'forgot itself'!

questions.question: What is the structure of accidental/unintentional se?

answers.text: se + indirect object pronoun + verb (3rd person)

questions.hint: Se me cayó, Se te rompió, Se nos perdió - follows this pattern.

questions.question: 'Se te cayó el libro' means...
questions.hint: Accidental se: Se + te + cayó = 'it fell on you' (you accidentally dropped it).

questions.question: 'Se nos perdieron las llaves' - Why is 'perdieron' plural?

answers.text: All accidental se verbs are plural
It's an error, should be singular

questions.hint: In accidental se, verb agrees with what was lost/broken: llaves (plural).

questions.question: 'Se habla español' means...
questions.hint: Passive se construction: Se habla = 'is spoken' (no agent specified).

questions.question: 'Se venden casas' - Why is 'venden' plural?
questions.hint: Passive se: verb agrees with subject. Casas (plural) → venden (plural).

questions.question: 'Se necesitan trabajadores' means...
questions.hint: Passive se: Trabajadores (plural subject) are needed.

questions.question: 'Se come bien aquí' means...

answers.text: One eats well here / The food is good here (impersonal)

questions.hint: Impersonal se: general 'one/you/people' - no specific subject.

questions.question: What is the verb form in impersonal se constructions?
questions.hint: Impersonal se uses SINGULAR verb: Se vive bien, Se trabaja mucho.

questions.question: 'Se necesita experiencia' vs 'Se necesita trabajar' - Which is which?

answers.text: First is passive (experiencia = subject); Second is impersonal (no subject)
First is impersonal; Second is passive

questions.hint: Passive has noun subject (experiencia). Impersonal has no subject (trabajar is infinitive).

questions.question: 'Se dice que...' means...

answers.text: It is said that... / People say that... (impersonal)

questions.hint: Impersonal se: general statement, no specific person saying it.

questions.question: Which verb changes meaning with reflexive pronoun: ponerse?
questions.hint: Poner = put/place something. Ponerse = put on (clothing) or become (state).
